flagged_sentences: In 1994, after the patent on the painkiller diclofenac expired, Indian generic manufacturers began selling the drug at low cost for treating cattle.

Using the natural experiment of districts that historically differed in vulture habitat suitability, economists Eyal Frank and Anant Sudarshan estimated in the American Economic Review that all-cause human mortality rose 4.7 percent in high-suitability districts between 2000 and 2005—an average of more than 100,000 additional deaths per year.

claims.claim: Widespread veterinary use of diclofenac in India began in 1994 after the patent lapsed.
claims.episode_span: In 1994, after the patent on the painkiller diclofenac expired, Indian generic manufacturers began selling the drug at low cost for treating cattle.
claims.source_title: The Population Decline of Gyps Vultures in India and Nepal Has Slowed since Veterinary Use of Diclofenac was Banned
claims.supporting_quote: Populations of oriental white-backed vulture (Gyps bengalensis), long-billed vulture (Gyps indicus) and slender-billed vulture (Gyps tenuirostris) crashed during the mid-1990s throughout the Indian subcontinent.

claims.claim: By 2007 India's oriental white-backed vulture population had fallen to roughly 0.1 percent of early-1990s levels.
claims.episode_span: By 2007 the oriental white-backed vulture had declined to 0.1 percent of its early-1990s numbers, according to repeated road-transect surveys reported in PLOS One.
claims.source_title: The Population Decline of Gyps Vultures in India and Nepal Has Slowed since Veterinary Use of Diclofenac was Banned
claims.supporting_quote: Surveys in India, initially conducted in 1991–1993 and repeated in 2000, 2002, 2003 and 2007, revealed that the population of Gyps bengalensis had fallen by 2007 to 0.1% of its numbers in the early 1990s.

claims.claim: Eyal Frank and Anant Sudarshan estimated in the American Economic Review that human mortality rose 4.7 percent in high vulture-habitat districts between 2000 and 2005, averaging more than 100,000 additional deaths per year.
claims.episode_span: Using the natural experiment of districts that historically differed in vulture habitat suitability, economists Eyal Frank and Anant Sudarshan estimated in the American Economic Review that all-cause human mortality rose 4.7 percent in high-suitability districts between 2000 and 2005—an average of more than 100,000 additional deaths per year.
claims.source_title: The Social Costs of Keystone Species Collapse: Evidence from the Decline of Vultures in India
claims.supporting_quote: Uses a natural experiment comparing districts with high vs. low historical vulture habitat suitability to estimate that vulture collapse increased all-cause human mortality rates by 4.7% (over 100,000 additional deaths per year) from 2000–2005

claims.claim: India banned veterinary diclofenac in 2006 and strengthened the prohibition in 2008.
claims.episode_span: India banned veterinary diclofenac in 2006 and strengthened the prohibition in 2008.
claims.source_title: Effectiveness of Action in India to Reduce Exposure of Gyps Vultures to the Toxic Veterinary Drug Diclofenac
claims.supporting_quote: The governments of India, Pakistan and Nepal took action in 2006 to prevent the veterinary use of diclofenac on domesticated livestock, the route by which contamination occurs.
